documents.generated_document: HOSPITAL NAME: Apex Cardiology Clinic. DEPARTMENT: Outpatient Cardiology. PATIENT NAME: Robert Jenkins. MRN: 9938210. DOB: 04/12/1955. AGE: 68. SEX: Male. ENCOUNTER DATE: 10/24/2023. DOCUMENT TYPE: Outpatient Progress Note. PROVIDER: Dr. Sarah Lin, MD. --- CHIEF COMPLAINT: Worsening shortness of breath and leg swelling. HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: The patient is a 68-year-old established male with a history of ischemic cardiomyopathy (HFrEF, EF 30%), CAD, and CKD stage 3, presenting today with a 1-week history of progressively worsening dyspnea on exertion, now occurring at rest. He reports 3-pillow orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, and an 8-pound weight gain over the last 5 days. He denies chest pain, palpitations, or syncope. Medication compliance is reported as good. REVIEW OF SYSTEMS: Cardiovascular: Positive for orthopnea and leg edema. Negative for chest pain. Respiratory: Positive for shortness of breath. All other systems reviewed and are negative. PHYSICAL EXAMINATION: Vitals: BP 152/92, HR 98, RR 24, Temp 98.6F, SpO2 91% on room air. General: Mild respiratory distress, speaking in short sentences. Neck: JVD elevated to 9 cm H2O. Lungs: Crackles present in bilateral lower bases. Cardiovascular: Tachycardic, regular rhythm, S3 gallop present, no murmurs. Extremities: 3+ pitting edema bilaterally up to the knees. DIAGNOSTIC DATA REVIEWED: Point-of-care EKG shows normal sinus rhythm with LVH, no acute ST-T wave changes. Point-of-care BNP is markedly elevated at 1450 pg/mL (baseline 450). BMP shows Creatinine 1.9 mg/dL (baseline 1.5), Potassium 4.3 mEq/L. ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: 1. Acute on chronic systolic heart failure exacerbation: High complexity and high risk of morbidity. The patient is on the verge of requiring inpatient admission. We will attempt aggressive outpatient diuresis first. Plan: Increase Furosemide from 40 mg daily to 80 mg BID for the next 3 days. Strict 1.5L fluid restriction and 2g sodium diet. Patient is instructed to go to the Emergency Department immediately if symptoms worsen or if he develops chest pain. 2. Acute Kidney Injury on CKD Stage 3: Likely cardiorenal syndrome vs over-diuresis in the past, though currently volume overloaded. Will recheck BMP in 48 hours. 3. Follow-up: Scheduled for a mandatory telehealth check-in tomorrow and an in-person visit in 48 hours with repeat labs. TIME SPENT: Total time spent by the provider on the date of the encounter, including face-to-face evaluation, counseling, and non-face-to-face record review and care coordination, was 45 minutes. --- Electronically Signed By: Dr. Sarah Lin, MD. Date Signed: 10/24/2023 15:30. End of Report.
